AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a brown material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings
   B. Fresh weeds
   C. Dry leaves
   D. Fresh cow dung

2. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To stop it from rotting
   C. To hide it from animals only
   D. To keep off rain and sun

3. Why should the drip container be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   B. To increase evaporation
   C. To warm the water
   D. To make water sweet

4. Why does drip irrigation save water? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more water than a hose
   B. Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   C. It waters at midday
   D. It wets the paths between plants

5. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It creates rain
   B. It makes the walls bigger
   C. It gives off a poisonous gas
   D. It makes the room too cold

6. Which of these is a fuel used at home for cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Sand
   C. Charcoal
   D. Cloth

7. Why should food be cut into small pieces before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   B. They burn the pot
   C. They take longer to cook
   D. They need more water

8. Why is poison a bad way to deal with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. It is too slow to spread
   B. It makes crops grow
   C. It is too cheap
   D. It can also kill other animals and people

9. What is used to make the arms of a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A shorter stick tied across the pole
   B. Sand
   C. A bottle
   D. A bucket of water

10. What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Water the bed so the soil is soft
   B. Cover it with plastic
   C. Cut the tops off
   D. Dry the bed

11. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   B. The plants are green and soft
   C. The plant flowers
   D. The seeds are wet

12. Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly? (1 mark)
   A. Millet
   B. Pawpaw tree
   C. Coconut
   D. Avocado

13. About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 cm
   B. Touching each other
   C. 5 metres
   D. About 1 mm

14. Why should tiny seeds not be sown deeply? (1 mark)
   A. They grow faster
   B. They wash away
   C. They become large
   D. They run out of stored food before reaching the light

15. Why should you avoid climbing thin branches while harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. They are too high
   B. They are cold
   C. They are too sweet
   D. They can break and you may fall

16. How does eating fruit help our health? (1 mark)
   A. It gives only sugar and nothing else
   B. It stops us drinking water
   C. It gives vitamins and fibre
   D. It makes us weak

17. How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag? (1 mark)
   A. By cutting the roots
   B. Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   C. By pulling the stem hard
   D. By throwing it

18. Why does passion fruit need a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   B. It eats insects
   C. It grows underground
   D. It is a tree

19. Which of these is an indigenous chicken called in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kienyeji
   B. Layer only
   C. Broiler
   D. Turkey

20. Which animal browses on leaves and shoots from bushes? (1 mark)
   A. Duck
   B. Goat
   C. Rabbit only
   D. Hen

21. What do protective foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Give all the body's energy
   B. Help the body to fight sickness
   C. Store water
   D. Build walls

22. Which food group gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Water only
   B. Protective foods only
   C. Energy-giving foods
   D. Salt

23. Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan? (1 mark)
   A. A sieve
   B. A ladle only
   C. A spatula
   D. A bucket

24. Which food may be served with boiled potatoes for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Soda only
   B. A second helping of potatoes only
   C. Sugar
   D. Vegetable stew

25. Which food is usually shallow fried? (1 mark)
   A. Tea
   B. Boiled maize
   C. Boiled rice
   D. Eggs

26. How should drinking water be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a clean container with a lid
   B. On the ground
   C. In an open basin
   D. With a dirty cup

27. What can be used if there is no soap? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Clean ash and running water
   C. Sugar
   D. Mud

28. Which PPE protects the nose and mouth from dust? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gloves
   C. Overall
   D. Gumboots

29. Why do we sweep before mopping? (1 mark)
   A. To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud
   B. To use more soap
   C. Because mops cannot touch water
   D. To waste time

30. How should broken glass be disposed of? (1 mark)
   A. Thrown in the yard
   B. Put in the compost
   C. Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   D. Left on the floor

31. Where should clean PPE be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a dry, clean place
   B. In a wet corner
   C. In a dirty box
   D. On the floor

32. Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes lighter
   B. It becomes cleaner
   C. It grows mould and smells
   D. It becomes stronger

33. What do you use to scrub gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. A heavy stone
   B. A hammer
   C. A soft brush with soapy water
   D. A knife

34. Which PPE protects the hands? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gumboots
   C. Gloves
   D. Headgear

35. What is the first step in cleaning gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. Dry them in strong sun
   B. Store them wet
   C. Knock off lumps of mud outside
   D. Put them in the fire

36. Which of these is another tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Long and short tacking
   B. Blanket stitch
   C. Herringbone
   D. French knot

37. What is one purpose of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. To cut cloth
   B. To wash cloth
   C. To iron cloth
   D. To hold layers of cloth together before sewing

38. What should you never do with a needle? (1 mark)
   A. Thread it
   B. Put it in your mouth
   C. Keep it in a pin cushion
   D. Use a thimble

39. How do you place pins for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Across the line
   B. Along the line
   C. Only at the edge
   D. Not at all

40. Why should you tie a knot in the thread before tacking? (1 mark)
   A. To make the cloth stiffer
   B. So the needle does not move
   C. So that the thread stays in the cloth
   D. To make the thread thicker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)

42. Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest. (5 marks)

43. Explain why a scarecrow becomes less useful if it is never moved. (3 marks)

44. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)

45. Name two problems that can attack ripe fruits. (2 marks)

46. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)

47. Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep. (3 marks)

48. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

49. Give three uses of tacking stitches. (3 marks)

50. Describe how to make even tacking. (4 marks)

51. Give three ways of disposing of refuse safely. (3 marks)

52. Describe how to make a tippy tap. (4 marks)

53. Explain how mulch and compost help a young fruit tree. (4 marks)

54. Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from. (3 marks)

55. Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day. (3 marks)

56. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)

57. Name two other ways of saving water in the garden. (2 marks)

58. Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe? (2 marks)

59. What is personal protective equipment (PPE)? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Dry leaves
   Brown materials are dry, like dry leaves, dry grass and straw.

2. D — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

3. A — To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   A cover keeps water clean and stops mosquitoes breeding.

4. B — Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   Only the soil near the plant is wet, so less water is lost.

5. C — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

6. C — Charcoal
   Charcoal is burnt to give heat.

7. A — Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   Small pieces heat through quickly.

8. D — It can also kill other animals and people
   Poison harms living things that are not the target.

9. A — A shorter stick tied across the pole
   The cross stick forms shoulders and arms.

10. A — Water the bed so the soil is soft
   Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

11. A — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

12. A — Millet
   Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

13. A — About 5 cm
   Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

14. D — They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   Deep seeds cannot push up to the surface.

15. D — They can break and you may fall
   Safety while picking fruit.

16. C — It gives vitamins and fibre
   Fruits protect the body and help digestion.

17. B — Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   Broken roots harm the seedling.

18. A — Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   Climbers need supports.

19. A — Kienyeji
   Kienyeji chickens are local breeds.

20. B — Goat
   Goats browse on shrubs.

21. B — Help the body to fight sickness
   Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

22. C — Energy-giving foods
   Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

23. C — A spatula
   A spatula lifts and turns food.

24. D — Vegetable stew
   Vegetables add protective foods.

25. D — Eggs
   Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

26. A — In a clean container with a lid
   Covering keeps germs out.

27. B — Clean ash and running water
   Ash helps to remove dirt when soap is not available.

28. A — Dust mask
   A dust mask covers the nose and mouth.

29. A — To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud
   Mopping dirt makes mud.

30. C — Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   This prevents cuts.

31. A — In a dry, clean place
   Damp PPE grows mould.

32. C — It grows mould and smells
   Moulds grow in damp places.

33. C — A soft brush with soapy water
   A soft brush avoids damage.

34. C — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

35. C — Knock off lumps of mud outside
   This removes the dirt before washing.

36. A — Long and short tacking
   Long and short tacking is another type.

37. D — To hold layers of cloth together before sewing
   Tacking keeps layers in place.

38. B — Put it in your mouth
   Needles are dangerous in the mouth.

39. A — Across the line
   Pins across the line hold the layers.

40. C — So that the thread stays in the cloth
   A knot stops the thread pulling through.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds and animals soon notice it never moves, learn that it is harmless, and come back to eat the crops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for noticing, 1 mark for learning it is harmless, 1 mark for returning to the crops.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fruit flies, birds or monkeys (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; bring the needle up; make 1 cm stitches with 1 cm gaps along the line; keep the thread loose; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Compost organic waste; put other waste in a bin with a lid and take it to a collection point; reuse or recycle paper, plastic and glass; wrap broken glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces weeds and protects roots from heat. Compost feeds the tree and improves soil structure.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for mulch, 2 marks for compost.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each tool with material.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Clothing and gear worn to protect the body from dirt, injury, dust and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for clothing or gear, 1 mark for protection.
